[RCLI.1.11] **The bundled library sits beside the compiler.** A compiler finds the library it ships with ([LIMP.3.3.1]) at
`../share/ds/stdlib`, resolved against the directory that holds its own
executable, and searches it after every `-L` directory, in the order
[RCLI.1.3] gives them. No option, environment variable or configuration names
that directory or removes it from the search path.

**A symbolic link to the compiler is followed.** The directory that holds the
executable is the one that holds the file itself, with every link on the way to
it resolved, so a compiler invoked through a link finds the library beside the
link's target and not beside the link. A chain of links that ends nowhere, or
that does not end, is a compiler that does not find the library (below).

Every build of a compiler **must** lay the library out there, whatever the build
is for. A compiler that runs with no file system of its own, such as one
compiled to WebAssembly, **must** present the library at that path in the file
system it reads.

**A compiler that does not find it resolves nothing.** `units.core` is read from
the library on every compilation ([LUNI.4.1.2]), so without it the compiler
would accept a different language. The compiler **must** refuse every
invocation that resolves a name with exit `2` ([RCLI.3.1]), naming the directory
it looked in. `dump-ast`, which resolves none ([RCLI.1.10]), is unaffected.
